answer: Like a coral reef that only grows where real polyps settle, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a small time-vested stake before transacting. A newcomer proves its stake with a cipher-based attestation bound to one hardware key, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs thousands of stakes. Reputation then flows like an ocean current: peers attest only agents whose work they verified, and trust decays unless renewed by useful service. Forging an army becomes prohibitively expensive, while honest agents earn standing cheaply through real work.
